source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"An improvement in the client's oxygenation with fairly little accompanying risk during a prolonged suction pass","B":"Hypoxia, since suctioning removes oxygen along with secretions, and prolonged suctioning increases this risk","C":"Essentially no physiological effect of any kind on the client, regardless of how long the suction pass lasts","D":"An increase in how much respiratory secretion the client's airway actually produces afterward"}}
source_row.rationale: Limiting each tracheostomy suction pass to a brief duration (generally no more than about 10-15 seconds per pass) is important because suctioning removes oxygen along with secretions, and prolonged suctioning increases the risk of significant hypoxia during the procedure.
source_row.source_detail: Rationale for Limited Suction Pass Duration
